summary.text: Frank Burns is a Democratic state representative from Delaware who has represented House District 21 since November 2024 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A scientist with a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania, he founded a biotechnology company in 2019.

paragraphs.text: Burns was born in Chicago, Illinois, and earned a bachelor's degree from Villanova University in 1981 and a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania in 1986.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he grew up in a working-poor household, was the first generation in his family to attend college, and earned his Ph.D. in biochemistry at the University of Pennsylvania School of Medicine with a pre-doctoral fellowship from the National Institutes of Health.

He said he was a medical school professor for more than a decade, joined the biotechnology company Qualicon in Wilmington in 2003, and in 2019 formed a biotechnology company focused on beneficial microbes.
He also said he volunteered with RespondDE during the COVID-19 pandemic, volunteers with the Food Bank of Delaware, and serves on the board of the Unitarian Universalist Society of Mill Creek.
Burns ran for House District 21 in 2022 and lost to Republican incumbent Michael Ramone, 4,346 votes to 4,381.
In 2024 he won the Democratic primary over Michael A. Smith and then defeated Republican Brenda Mennella in the general election, taking office on November 6, 2024.
For the 2025-2026 session he was assigned to the Health & Human Development, Labor, Natural Resources and Energy, Transportation, and Veterans Affairs committees.

In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey, he listed his campaign priorities as education funding, including universal pre-K and free school breakfast and lunch, green energy and biologically based industries, and affordable housing.
